display_name: Large Module Creation and Refactor Protocol
description: Canonical generic behavior-preserving large-module decomposition law and KANDA specialist dispatcher.
do_not_regress: Keep ideal module size at 400 physical lines or fewer and the absolute hard maximum at 500 physical lines or fewer.
Split by cohesive responsibility rather than arbitrary line ranges.
Do not impose a universal 101-line minimum or create unnecessary micro-files.
Preserve public imports, signatures, decorators, exceptions, side effects, consumers, and observable behavior.
Use exact current source identity and current consumer/public-contract evidence before choosing architecture.
Keep dependency direction one-way and prohibit cross-Box private reach-in.
Validate every touched permanent source module and require rollback to the exact predecessor.
Delegate KANDA Planner, Workbench, AST repair, delivery, terminal, evidence, and freeze mechanics to their current owners.
Preserve PEP 8 compliance and count physical lines only after normal readable formatting.
Preserve SOLID responsibility/dependency design during every split.
Preserve one authoritative DRY implementation owner for each behavior.
Create cohesive helpers when the hard maximum or current responsibility evidence requires decomposition.
When decomposition is required, create cohesive helpers rather than compressing or padding source.
Route post-refactor unresolved-name, binding, boundary, smoke, and cohesion evidence to current validators; do not recreate a universal fragmentation runner.
